atlas-mt.0060: There is no single graduate season. Deloitte Malta’s Graduate Programme takes people who finished their studies within the last year or finish within 12 months; its team was at the students’ union Freshers’ Week stand on 5–7 October 2026. A bet365 trainee listing ran only from 4 to 19 November 2025.
atlas-mt.0061: Internships follow the academic year: Betsson’s MCAST infosec internship is full time from July to September and part time, 10 to 20 hours a month, from October to May.
atlas-mt.0062: Employers name two local feeders: the University of Malta and MCAST. Deloitte’s student hub lists an Undergraduate Programme for university students and internship and apprenticeship programmes for MCAST students, and HSBC Malta’s summer interns came from the University, MCAST’s Institute of Business Management and Commerce, and JA Malta.
atlas-mt.0063: The students’ union (KSU) holds a Careers’ Expo on campus in spring (an exhibitor post is dated 10 March 2026); Bank of Valletta met students at a three-day Careers Expo at the University of Malta in March 2023.
atlas-mt.0064: iGaming industry events in Malta, such as those of SiGMA, are where many first contacts are made, and a Deloitte team member joins the KSU Freshers’ Week in early October.
atlas-mt.0065: The Big Four in Malta train graduates through sponsored ACCA programmes and have looked abroad, for example to Greek graduates, to fill places; the funds and gaming industries keep audit demand high.
atlas-mt.0066: Deloitte’s International Graduate Programme places recent accounting graduates in Audit & Assurance with a relocation allowance and a permanent contract, and you apply through its job search page.
atlas-mt.0067: Finance and insurance are 5.1% of Malta’s jobs, against 2.3% in the EU. Bank of Valletta runs a Graduates’ Programme, and HSBC Malta takes summer interns.
atlas-mt.0068: The MFSA had 575 staff in 2025, 45 of them students in its Pre-Graduate Programme, and works with the University of Malta on a postgraduate programme in financial regulation and compliance. The Malta Gaming Authority takes student interns.
atlas-mt.0069: More than 300 iGaming firms operate from Malta; the industry body works with MCAST and the University of Malta on a student placement scheme that feeds developers and analysts into it.
atlas-mt.0070: Betsson’s one-year paid infosec internship, posted by the MCAST ICT Institute, works with the Information Security Governance Team on governance, risk and compliance.
atlas-mt.0071: No national season: employers recruit when they have a vacancy, and Jobsplus lists them all year. Programme windows are short and set by each employer, such as bet365’s two weeks in November 2025.
atlas-mt.0072: The programmes read ask for a first degree: Bank of Valletta takes MQF level 6 or above and bet365 a 2:1 gained within three years. A postgraduate course matters for regulation and compliance, where the MFSA partners with the University of Malta. Recent graduates with a first degree already find work: 92.8% of those aged 20 to 34 were in work in 2025.
atlas-mt.0073: EU degrees go in as plain copies of certificates. For some work-permit routes (Specialist Employee Initiative, EU Blue Card) Malta’s qualifications recognition centre, MQRIC, validates a tertiary degree of at least three years; regulated professions need their own recognition.
atlas-mt.0074: Employers name the University of Malta and MCAST and nothing more, and no page read ranks schools. In a market this size the reputation that counts is the candidate’s own.
atlas-mt.0075: Deloitte offers an MCAST apprenticeship for students who must complete one as part of an advanced diploma or degree, and Betsson runs its infosec internship through MCAST.
atlas-mt.0076: Public administration, defence, education, health and social work employed 70,440 people in 2025, 20.8% of Malta’s 338,190 jobs, against 24.4% in the EU.
atlas-mt.0077: Employers hire from abroad: Deloitte runs an international programme with a relocation allowance, and Malta’s labour migration policy sets a workforce growth limit by company size. Rivermate notes that visa quotas and local rules can limit sponsorship. Rules are on the Visas page.
atlas-mt.0078: A photo is optional: Konnekt calls it unexpected and advises against it, and leaves out the date of birth.
atlas-mt.0079: EURES Malta says the CV is usually no longer than two pages; Konnekt advises one page for graduates and two for experienced candidates, as a PDF with a clear file name.
atlas-mt.0080: EURES asks for a brief covering letter of a few paragraphs, and the Malta Gaming Authority asks for a CV and covering letter for internships.
atlas-mt.0081: EURES lists references among the application documents, while Konnekt says to write that they are available on request and give contact details only when asked.
atlas-mt.0082: EURES says to send copies of certificates with the application, and typed documents; some employers use their own application form with open questions.
atlas-mt.0083: The Malta Gaming Authority says its offer is meant to meet the salary expectations candidates state at the start of the process, so be ready to name a figure early.
atlas-mt.0084: A law-firm guide says staff whose work relates directly to the gaming system must be vetted as fit and proper persons, and EURES says some jobs need a medical certificate before you start.
atlas-mt.0085: Word of mouth and recommendations carry real weight; in a small market a firm’s and a candidate’s reputation travel fast.
atlas-mt.0086: Employers do hire people still abroad: the policy has a “still abroad” application route, and Deloitte’s International Graduate Programme is built for it. A non-EU applicant should expect the employer’s advert and the labour market test before any permit.
atlas-mt.0087: English is an official language (with Maltese) and enough for most private-sector roles; Maltese matters in the public sector.
atlas-mt.0088: The Malta Gaming Authority describes five stages: a first interview, a task showing what the job involves, a second interview where you present the task, a behavioural profiling test, then the offer. Deloitte’s international programme starts with a first conversation arranged by a team member after you apply online.
atlas-mt.0089: No page read gives a time from application to offer. For a non-EU hire add the employer’s three-week advert on Jobsplus and EURES and the permit processing before a start date.
atlas-mt.0090: The CV is in English, and some jobs require a medical examination before employment.
atlas-mt.0091: Either a contract or a written statement of core conditions is required, covering the job, pay, hours, leave, probation and notice. Probation is six months as standard, up to a year for managerial or technical roles paid at least double the minimum wage.
atlas-mt.0092: In probation either side can end the job without a reason, with a week’s notice once you have worked more than a month; after that notice rises from one week to twelve weeks at ten years’ service.
atlas-mt.0093: Deloitte’s international programme offers a permanent job, a salary package and a relocation allowance; the Malta Gaming Authority aims the offer at the salary you named at the start. No page read says whether extra statutory months of pay apply or how long you have to decide.
atlas-mt.0094: For new non-EU hires the employer must advertise on Jobsplus and EURES for at least three weeks in the two months before applying; the period is two weeks for the Key Employee Initiative, Specialist Employee Initiative, EU Blue Card and Skilled Occupation List. Health, care, regulator-endorsed cases, sportspersons and change of employer are exempt.
atlas-mt.0095: The monthly labour market test looks back 12 months at the employer’s recruitment and redundancy record and the 2% disability quota, and caps growth through non-EU hires by size: up to 200% for firms of 1–9 staff, 100% for 10–49, 50% for 50–249 and 25% for 250 or more.
atlas-mt.0096: In practice this favours established employers with headcount to spare, such as the Big Four and gaming operators; raise your status at the first conversation, since the advert comes before the application.
atlas-mt.0097: Jobsplus, the national employment agency, runs the “Find a Job” portal, a traineeship scheme and the Youth Guarantee; vacancies posted there pass to EURES. Employer pages worth knowing: Deloitte’s “Join Deloitte” search, PwC’s student page, the Malta Gaming Authority’s Talexio portal and Betsson’s careers list.
atlas-mt.0098: Bank of Valletta takes enquiries for its Graduates’ Programme by email at resourcing-graduates@bov.com. Recruiters GRS Recruitment and Konnekt publish Malta job-search guides, and the KSU Careers’ Expo and Freshers’ Week are the campus events.
atlas-mt.0099: Sending a Europass CV to private employers: Konnekt says recruiters find it forgettable and keeps it for public-sector roles and EU bodies.
atlas-mt.0100: Assuming a non-EU offer is enough: the employer has to advertise the job on Jobsplus and EURES and pass the labour market test before a permit can be requested.
atlas-mt.0101: Waiting for a graduate season: programme windows are short, as with bet365’s two weeks in November 2025, so follow each employer’s page.
atlas-mt.0102: Leaving out your languages: Betsson’s Malta list asks for German, Danish, Nordic or Lithuanian beside English in customer roles, and EURES lists language proficiency as a CV section.
atlas-mt.0103: English is the working language of the programmes read: EURES asks for a CV written in English, and the Deloitte and Malta Gaming Authority pages are in English with no other language required.
atlas-mt.0104: The Deloitte International Graduate Programme page states no language requirement and is written in English.
